In late 1950, after UN forces (led by the US) nearly reached the Yalu River, China sent hundreds of thousands of troops across the border. They drove UN forces out of North Korea, recaptured Seoul briefly, then the front stabilized near the 38th parallel after UN counterattacks.

The July 1953 armistice created the DMZ along that final line. Outcome was a stalemate restoring the pre-war division. Chinese intervention did prevent North Korea's collapse.
